source.title: Annotation Entropy Predicts Per-Example Learning Dynamics in LoRA Fine-Tuning

record.tranche_reason: The study measures learning dynamics in LoRA fine-tuning on NLI, including a preliminary label-noise intervention, but does not test the claim versions about random-label fitting, training time, generalization, regularization, or learning real labels before random labels.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Arpit et al. on learning patterns before memorization, but its own experiments do not measure whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels. The preliminary noise-injection results are related to the claim's subject but do not establish any listed version.
record.test_reason: The study measures learning dynamics by annotation ambiguity and a small AULC shift after partial label corruption. It does not measure random-label fitting, time to convergence, or learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing corrupted labels. Naturally contested majority-vote labels are not established noisy or random labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but omits the central conclusion: annotation entropy predicts learning dynamics across six models and two NLI datasets, with positive correlations in all 25 conditions and 21 significant after correction. Contested examples exhibit increasing loss under LoRA, largely absent under full fine-tuning and IA3. The noise-injection experiment provides preliminary, small-effect evidence consistent with this account.
record.recipe_differences: LoRA fine-tuning of NLI models with partial label corruption; it does not use the original image-classification random-label fitting setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The AULC–entropy correlation is reported as stable across the tested 0%, 30%, and 60% label-noise conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing 30% or 60% of clean-example labels with uniform-random labels raises their mean AULC from 0.719 to 0.726 and 0.728. The reported effect is small (d=0.20), with paired per-example p<10^-8; entropy correlations remain approximately 0.31.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Partial label corruption modestly increases clean-category AULC during RoBERTa LoRA fine-tuning on SNLI without substantially changing its correlation with annotation entropy.

fits_no_version.finding: High-annotation-entropy examples have increasing loss under LoRA across six models, whereas full fine-tuning decreases loss across entropy groups and IA3 shows negligible contested-example loss change.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LoRA fine-tuning can increase loss on naturally ambiguous NLI training examples while improving high-agreement examples.

record.code_released: Code and per-example tracking data will be released upon acceptance.
record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The authors characterize the noise-injection experiment as preliminary and the effect size as small. It uses synthetic corruption, one model and task setting, and reports AULC shifts rather than fit accuracy on corrupted labels or the order in which clean and corrupted examples are learned.
record.rows_left_out: No results measuring the listed claim versions were reported. The three noise-injection results are included as related findings under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Time required to fit random versus true labels and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions; AULC alone does not measure either.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily increasing test error across label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and generalization with true labels.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels. Neither ambiguity-group trajectories nor the corruption experiment identify this temporal sequence.

record.verdict_notes: The authors' comparison with patterns-before-memorization work does not itself test V6: linguistic disagreement is treated as genuine ambiguity, and the study does not track subsequent memorization of identified corrupted labels.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting, test error at chance, and unchanged architecture or training hyperparameters.
Training-time cost of fitting random labels and convergence speed across corruption levels.
Perfect training fit and test-error progression across random-label corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether networks learn shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels, and how the two are learned over training.

rows.subject: RoBERTa, LoRA r=4
rows.operation_detail: Replace 30% of clean-example labels with uniform-random labels and measure AULC.
rows.note: The study describes this as a small upward shift in AULC; it does not report fitting accuracy on the corrupted examples.
rows.check: The values and conditions match the text, but increased aggregate AULC does not establish convergence speed, fitting accuracy, or real-before-noise learning order. The reported small effect is significant, but cannot be classified as partial realization of any listed version.

rows.subject: RoBERTa, LoRA r=4
rows.operation_detail: Measure the AULC–entropy correlation at three label-noise levels.
rows.note: The paper says the correlation remains stable across the reported noise levels; the outcome is a learning-dynamics correlation, not random-label fit or memorization order.
rows.check: The reported correlations match the text. Stability of the AULC–annotation-entropy relationship cannot establish any listed version's effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
